newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to allow mutuals, banks mergers.
newsitem.headline: Australia to allow mutuals, banks mergers.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday the government would allow mergers between mutual societies and banks.
"The six pillars policy is abolished and there is no restriction on mergers between mutuals and banks," Costello told reporters after releasing Australia's financial system inquiry.

Costello announced the government's initial response to the inquiry, including the end of the so-called six pillars policy which had banned mergers between the four major banks and two leading life insurance companies.
But he said mergers between the banks would not be allowed at this stage, but would depend on new competition.
Costello said he planned to announce further government responses to the inquiry's findings after the 1997/98 budget, due to be released on May 13.
Australia's big four National Australia Bank Ltd, Westpac Banking Corp, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, and the Australian and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd.
The two life offices included the six pillars policy is the Australia Mutual Provident Society (AMP) and National Mutual Holdings Ltd.
